paragraphs.text: Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia is a neonatal lethal form of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (SMD). Its features are severe metaphyseal chondrodysplasia with mild limb shortening, platyspondyly, cardiac conduction defects, and central nervous system abnormalities (Smith et al., 2014).

paragraphs.text: Sedaghatian (1980) reported 2 brothers, born within a year of each other, who had the same skeletal disorder: severe congenital metaphyseal involvement, mild rhizomelic shortness of the upper limbs, and mild platyspondyly. Both died at 3 days of age of cardiorespiratory insufficiency. Only one had laboratory tests before death, which showed low calcium, high phosphorus, and high alkaline phosphatase levels. At autopsy, this infant had pulmonary, renal, and adrenal hemorrhage, subendocardial myocarditis, and myocardial necrosis. The parents were normal and later had an affected daughter.

paragraphs.text: Koutouby et al. (2000) reported an infant with spondylometaphyseal dysplasia born to nonconsanguineous Yemeni parents. The radiologic findings were consistent with lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia of the Sedaghatian type. All previously reported patients had died within 4 days of life, but this patient survived 161 days. Extensive investigations were performed, and analysis of genomic DNA from the patient and parents did not identify an abnormal gene.

paragraphs.text: English et al. (2006) reported a girl with Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia born to nonconsanguineous Caucasian parents. She had metaphyseal dysplasia, was hypotonic from birth, and had recurrent cyanotic episodes starting within a few hours of delivery. Cerebral imaging showed absence of the corpus callosum and marked frontotemporal pachygyria. She developed seizures on day 14 of life and died at 17 days of age. English et al. (2006) suggested that the disorder may be associated with neuronal migration abnormalities and proposed a novel association with agenesis of the corpus callosum.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2014) performed whole-exome sequencing in a girl with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia and her unaffected parents. They found 2 rare variants in the GPX4 gene (138322): c.587+5G-A, inherited from the mother, and c.588-8_588-4del, which had arisen de novo (NM_001039848.1). Both variants were predicted to affect splicing. In vitro studies showed that the 2 splice mutations caused splicing out of part of exon 4 and skipping of exon 5, respectively. Both resulted in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.

checks.claim: The girl with SMDS reported by Smith et al. (2014) was compound heterozygous for the GPX4 c.588-8_588-4del mutation and a maternally inherited GPX4 c.587+5G-A mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The first (c.587+5G>A) was inherited from the mother, and the second (c.588-8_588-4del) was de novo (NM_001039848.1)
checks.explanation: Compound heterozygosity is implied but not explicitly stated or phase-confirmed in the abstract.

checks.claim: The GPX4 c.588-8_588-4del and c.587+5G-A mutations were both predicted to affect splicing.
checks.evidence_quote: both were predicted to impact splicing of GPX4

checks.claim: In vitro studies showed that the GPX4 c.587+5G-A mutation caused splicing out of part of exon 4.
checks.evidence_quote: In vitro studies confirmed the mutations spliced out part of exon 4 and skipped exon 5, respectively

checks.claim: In vitro studies showed that the GPX4 c.588-8_588-4del mutation caused skipping of exon 5.
checks.evidence_quote: In vitro studies confirmed the mutations spliced out part of exon 4 and skipped exon 5, respectively

checks.claim: The GPX4 c.588-8_588-4del and c.587+5G-A mutations both resulted in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.
checks.evidence_quote: with both resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2014) studied a child with SMDS whose DNA was not available. Sanger sequencing showed that both unaffected parents were heterozygous for the same c.381C-A transversion in exon 3 of the GPX4 gene (NM_001039848.1), which results in a tyr127-to-ter (Y127X) substitution.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2014) studied a child with SMDS whose DNA was not available.
checks.evidence_quote: a second child with SSMD was identified; although DNA from the child was not available

checks.claim: Sanger sequencing showed that both unaffected parents of the child with SMDS studied by Smith et al. (2014) were heterozygous for the same GPX4 c.381C-A transversion in exon 3 (NM_001039848.1).
checks.evidence_quote: the two unaffected parents were found by Sanger sequencing to each carry the same heterozygous stop mutation in exon 3 of GPX4, c.381C>A, p.Tyr127* (NM_001039848.1)
checks.explanation: Stated directly; C>A is a transversion.

checks.claim: The GPX4 c.381C-A transversion results in a tyr127-to-ter (Y127X) substitution.
